definition: The traditional Iranian weight unit for wholesale gold trading.
notes: Exactly 4.6083 g. The unit the Market Quote (mazanneh) is expressed in. Not the same as the Arabian mithqal (4.25 g) - do not convert with a foreign constant.

definition: The retail unit of weight; all consumer sales and jewelry invoices are per gram.
notes: Wholesale quotes in Mesghal are converted to gram for retail: gram = mesghal / 4.6083.

definition: Shop-floor subunit of the gram used when weighing small jewelry pieces.
notes: 1 sut = 0.001 g, i.e. the third decimal place on a jeweler's scale. Money amounts must never be rounded before weight is resolved to sut precision.

definition: The gold content of an alloy, stated either in karat (out of 24) or as fineness per 1000.
notes: Store fineness per 1000 as the canonical value (integer, e.g. 750) and derive karat for display. Karat and the gemstone 'carat' (weight) are different concepts - never share a type.

definition: Effectively pure gold, the reference purity all other alloys are stated against.
notes: 999.9 fineness. Used as the valuation basis; rarely sold as jewelry because it is too soft.

definition: Gold alloy of 750/1000 fineness, the standard retail purity for gold sold to consumers in Iran.
notes: 18/24 = 0.750 fine. The per-gram retail unit of account; retail invoices are metal value at the 18k gram rate + making charge + profit + VAT.

definition: Recast (re-melted) gold traded as unmarked bullion in the wholesale market, sold by weight rather than by piece.
notes: Trade unit is the Mesghal. Market-standard fineness is ~705 (17 karat); an assay certificate accompanies each lot. This is the instrument the Market Quote is quoted against.

definition: A mint-marked, serial-numbered gold bar sold by weight with an assay certificate.
notes: Distinct from melted_gold: a bar is branded and certified, so it carries its own premium. Sold in fixed weights.

definition: Any minted gold coin traded as a unit of bullion, priced per piece rather than per gram.
notes: Umbrella term. Never use alone in code where a specific coin type is meant; use the specific id.

definition: The post-1979 full Bahar Azadi gold coin bearing the Imam Khomeini design; the market's benchmark coin.
notes: Gross weight 8.133 g, fineness 900 (21.6 karat) => 7.3224 g fine gold. Quoted separately from the old design and normally at a higher premium.

definition: The earlier Bahar Azadi full coin design, quoted separately from the Emami coin.
notes: Same metal spec as emami_coin (8.133 g, fineness 900) but a different quoted price - the gap is collector/design premium, not metal.

definition: The full (one-unit) denomination of the Bahar Azadi coin series, as opposed to the half and quarter denominations.
notes: 8.133 g, fineness 900. 'Full' names the DENOMINATION; 'Emami' vs 'old design' names the MINT DESIGN. See the open question in ubiquitous-language.md.

definition: The half-unit denomination of the Bahar Azadi series.
notes: 4.0665 g, fineness 900. Carries a higher premium per gram than the full coin.

definition: The quarter-unit denomination of the Bahar Azadi series.
notes: 2.0332 g, fineness 900. Premium per gram is higher again than the half coin.

definition: The smallest minted denomination, roughly one gram.
notes: ~1.016 g, fineness 900. Highest premium per gram of the coin family; behaves more like a gift item than bullion.

definition: Crafted, wearable gold pieces, typically gemstone-set, priced from metal value plus making charge plus stone valuation.
notes: Distinct from bullion: price is not a pure function of weight. Reserve this term for gemstone/crafted goods.

definition: Gold bought back from a customer, valued on metal content alone.
notes: No making charge is paid on buy-back and a deduction for melt loss may apply. Its own valuation path - never price it through the retail formula.

aka: gold delivery note; deferred delivery receipt
definition: A transferable claim on a quantity of gold held by a dealer, settled or delivered later.
notes: A claim, not metal. Carries counterparty risk and must be modelled as a position against an issuer, never as inventory on hand.

definition: The market's headline benchmark price: the price of one Mesghal of 17-karat melted gold, from which most other domestic gold prices are derived.
notes: Quoted per Mesghal, not per gram. The 18k gram rate is derived from it. Treat as a rate, never as a product.

definition: The international spot price of one troy ounce of gold in USD.
notes: 1 troy ounce = 31.1035 g. Together with the USD rate it drives the domestic quote; it is an external input, refreshed on its own cadence.

definition: The USD/IRR rate the market prices gold against.
notes: The second external input. Domestic price moves are attributable to either this or the global ounce - keep them separate so the cause of a move stays visible.

definition: The fee charged for crafting a piece, quoted as a percentage of its metal value.
notes: Set per piece by design and workshop, not fixed market-wide. Paid on sale, never refunded on buy-back. VAT applies to this component.

definition: The dealer's margin, applied on top of metal value plus making charge.
notes: Typically a percentage. VAT applies to this component.

definition: Value-added tax on a retail gold sale.
notes: Under current Iranian law VAT is levied on the making charge and margin ONLY, not on the metal value. Encoding it as a flat percentage of the invoice total is a defect.

definition: The excess of a coin's market price over the value of the gold it contains.
notes: premium = market price - (fine gold weight x gram rate). Can go negative. The primary signal traders watch on coins; must be computed, never stored as an input.

definition: The price at which the dealer BUYS from the customer - i.e. the customer's selling price.
notes: Perspective trap: 'buy rate' on a shop board is the shop's buy. Always name prices from the DEALER's side in code and label them from the customer's side in the UI.

definition: The price at which the dealer SELLS to the customer - i.e. the customer's purchase price.
notes: Always higher than dealer_bid; the gap is the spread. Same perspective rule as dealer_bid.
